uccSellerRemedies.name: UCC Seller's Remedies

remedies.rule: Resell goods and recover difference from contract price (§ 2-706)
remedies.formula: Contract price - Resale price + Incidental damages

remedies.rule: If no resale, recover contract-market differential (§ 2-708(1))
remedies.formula: Contract price - Market price + Incidental damages

remedies.rule: For lost volume sellers, recover lost profit (§ 2-708(2))
remedies.formula: Profit seller would have made + Incidental damages + Costs reasonably incurred

remedies.rule: Recover full price if goods accepted, lost/damaged after risk passed, or identified and cannot be resold (§ 2-709)
Stop delivery of goods in transit upon buyer's insolvency or repudiation

uccSellerRemedies.incidentalDamages: Expenses related to breach (storage, resale, transportation)
uccSellerRemedies.noConsequential: Seller generally cannot recover consequential damages under UCC
uccSellerRemedies.mnemonics: Seller's Remedies: RMLPS (Resale, Market, Lost profit, Price, Stoppage)
uccSellerRemedies.essayTips: Lost volume seller doctrine is frequently tested. Seller must mitigate. Price action is limited. No consequential damages for sellers (generally).
uccSellerRemedies.mbeTips: Lost volume seller gets profit, not just resale difference. Resale must be commercially reasonable. Price action requires inability to resell.

contractsKeyDistinctions.explanation: Common Law governs services and real property; UCC Article 2 governs goods. If mixed contract, majority test applies (what is predominant purpose).
Bilateral: exchange of promises; accepted by promise. Unilateral: promise for performance; accepted only by completing performance.
Express conditions require STRICT compliance. Implied/constructive conditions require only substantial performance.
Assignment transfers RIGHTS; delegation transfers DUTIES. Assignor remains liable unless novation; delegator always remains liable.
Offer creates power of acceptance; invitation (ads, price quotes) is just negotiation. Look for definiteness and intent to be bound.
Void = no legal effect from start (illegal, no capacity). Voidable = valid until avoided by party with right to avoid (minor, fraud, duress).
Material breach excuses other party's performance. Minor breach allows damages but doesn't excuse performance.
Impossibility: literally cannot perform. Impracticability: extremely burdensome. Frustration: can perform but purpose destroyed.
